chunks: My father (RA) narrated to us, he said: `Ali ibn Ibrahim narrated to us, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from `Abd Allah ibn Sinan, from Abu `Abd Allah (AS)

regarding the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: 'His Kursi extends over the heavens and the earth.' He (AS) said: 'The heavens and the earth, and whatever is between them, are in the Kursi, and the `Arsh is the Knowledge over which no one has power.'

key_terms.الْعَرْشُ: The Empyrean Throne, interpreted here as Divine Knowledge
key_terms.الْعِلْمُ: Knowledge, specifically Divine Knowledge in this context
key_terms.الْكُرْسِيِّ: The Throne or Seat, interpreted here as the container of the physical universe

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between the Kursi and the `Arsh according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from Shaykh al-Saduq’s *al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies the cosmological hierarchy by distinguishing between the physical containment of the universe within the Kursi and the metaphysical nature of the `Arsh as the vast, incomprehensible Divine Knowledge. This interpretation aligns with the Shia theological emphasis on *tanzih* (divine transcendence), asserting that the `Arsh is not a physical throne but a symbol of the boundless scope of Allah’s knowledge, which exceeds all created dimensions.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 2. My father (RA) said: `Ali ib Ibrahim said, on the authority of his father, on the authority of Ibn Abu `Umayr, on the authority of `Abd Allah ibn Sinan that Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS)

was asked to interpret the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: His knowledge extends over the heaves and the earth.’ He (AS) said: “The heavens and the earth, and whatever is between them, are in the Throne [al-kursi], and the Empyrean [al-`arsh] is the Knowledge (of Allah) over which no one has power.”
